thread:
anya: FYI escalating customer bug: batch rerank seems to shift scores when a query has an empty candidate list. Request id req_0a1b2c3d.

sam: Can you paste the sanitized request + response? Which model/version?

anya: Model: rerank-v2-2026-02. Payload below (sanitized).

anya: ```
{
  "batch_id": "cust-8420",
  "queries": ["q1","q2","q3","q4","q5","q6"],
  "candidates": [
    ["c1","c2"],
    [],
    ["c3","c4","c5"],
    ["c6"],
    ["c7","c8","c9"],
    ["c10"]
  ]
}

# service response (truncated)
{
  "scores": [0.9,0.1, 0.7,0.2,0.5, 0.6,0.3,0.4, 0.8],
  "per_query_counts": [2,0,3,1,3,1]
}
```

anya: Customer reports client mapped scores so q2 got [0.7,0.2] (which are q3 scores) — everything after that looks shifted.

sam: If client uses prefix sums on per_query_counts they should still slice fine when count==0. Did they rely on implicit offsets?

olivia: Customer code shows `offsets = prefix_sum(per_query_counts)` then `scores[offset:offset+count]`. They claim offsets were computed but values mismatched. They attached raw http exchange.

support-bot: Created RED-INC-2031, attached logs, assigned to @sam and @matt.

matt: Any transfer encoding or compression? We've seen gzipped payload edge cases.

anya: They used curl --data-binary with `Content-Encoding: gzip` (their SDK compresses payloads over threshold). Link to sanitized payload: https://redwood.internal/sup/att/req_0a1b2c3d

sam: Gzip streaming bugs usually cause parse errors, but maybe our flatten/encoder path mishandles empty lists.

matt: I repro locally. Steps: send batch with an empty candidate array, capture flattener + encoder logs. Observed: offsets computed correctly, but the flattened buffer write loop skips zero-length segments and our encoder's export loop uses a running index that doesn't increment for skipped segments -> downstream writer reads from wrong index -> subsequent scores shift. Off-by-one after empty slot.

sam: So it's server-side. Good. Short term mitigation for customer?

matt: Options: 1) Ask customer to avoid empty arrays or send a placeholder negative candidate (hacky). 2) We can ask them to rely on `per_query_counts` and remap if things look off (but that still assumes service counts are trustworthy). Better: patch server.

olivia: I replied to customer with: (A) temporary: don't send empty arrays or include dummy candidate, (B) we will patch and replay their anon payload in staging if they consent. Asked for permission to replay.

matt: Opened PR #4227 fixing the encoder loop (ensure running index increments for zero-counts and preserve empty segments). Added unit tests for candidate_count==0. Planning canary in staging today, prod tomorrow PST if green.

sam: Also adding a fuzz/regression test that generates random candidate lists including zeros.

anya: Customer allowed staging replay. They asked about billing/latency impact — told them no billing change, negligible latency except brief deploy window.

olivia: While the patch rolls out, I added a short-term server-side validation to reject empty candidate lists with HTTP 400 + clear message, to prevent silent misalignment for other callers. Not ideal but prevents data corruption until deploy. CS and billing notified.

sam: Good containment. Monitoring RED-INC-2031 and will post updates to #eng-ml.

anya: Thanks all, closing loop with customer. :thumbsup:
